forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Oadby and Wigston's five-year financial plan shows a deficit every year, with general reserves falling
news_drafts.lead:
Oadby and Wigston Borough Council's five-year financial plan projects a deficit in each year of the forecast period, and its general fund reserve, the cushion held for the unexpected, falls across the life of the plan. The figures are in the council's audited financial report and Annual Governance Statement for 2025/26, presented to its Audit Committee on 7 October 2026.

The plan, known as the medium-term financial plan, was approved in February 2026. It shows "budget gaps each year" even though the council has balanced its budget for 2026/27. The report says 2025/26 and 2026/27 were addressed through "substantial savings" made under the council's sustainability programme. The narrative also acknowledges that the underlying gap between what the council expects to spend and what it expects to have has not been closed.

The report puts the savings in a longer context. The council's budget has fallen from £8.5m in 2010/11 to £7.7m in 2025/26, a reduction of about 9%. The papers describe the plan as one that "projects deficits over the course of the 5-year forecast resulting in the General fund reserve decreasing over the life of the MTFP". They do not give the yearly gap or reserve figures in the material supplied.

findings.headline: Six Business Continuity audit findings from 2024/25 remain pending internal auditor follow-up 12 months after their original due dates.
findings.detail: Six audit actions from the 2024/25 Business Continuity audit had original deadlines between 30 June and 30 September 2025. All six remain marked 'IA to Follow-Up' as of 22 September 2026, including training needs assessment and Depot Services BCP testing, neither of which have updates recorded. The IT and Projects BCP was revised in April 2026 but also remains awaiting final follow-up.
findings.matters: A finance director at another council would want to observe how peers address slow audit remediation, as consistently overdue actions could indicate governance or organisational capacity constraints affecting financial management.
findings.figures: Six findings; original due dates 30/06/2025–30/09/2025; current status as at 22 September 2026

findings.headline: Three audit findings in Revenues and Benefits remain in pending remediation status with deadlines in December 2026 and June 2027.
findings.detail: The 2025/26 audit identified three matters in Revenues and Benefits requiring remediation: empty property quarterly review outputs, quality assurance procedures, and business continuity plan. All are marked as pending remediation as of 22 September 2026, with due dates of 31 December 2026 for the BCP and 30 June 2027 for the other two. Revenue collection is a critical income function for councils.
findings.matters: A lender would care about unresolved audit findings affecting revenue administration, as revenue collection is fundamental to the council's financial resilience and debt service capacity.
findings.figures: Three findings with due dates 31/12/2026 and 30/06/2027

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 - Audited Financial Report (2025/26) & Annual Governance Statement (2025/26)
findings.headline: Pension liability of £11.96m carries additional contribution rate of 22.4% plus £699k lump sum following March 2025 revaluation
findings.detail: The council's Local Government Pension Scheme liability stands at £11.96m. The scheme was revalued in March 2025, setting an additional contribution rate of '22.4% plus £699k' for 2025/26. The council contributed £1.95m to the scheme during 2025/26 and recognised a £0.78m charge. This additional rate means the council pays above-standard contributions to offset the pension deficit.
findings.matters: Pension contributions of 22.4% plus fixed costs represent a significant and growing embedded cost in the council's base budget that limits flexibility to redirect spending to emerging priorities
findings.figures: Pension liability £11.96m; additional contribution rate 22.4% plus £699k lump sum; total contributions paid £1.95m; year charge £0.78m
findings.quote: The last valuation took place in March 2025 which set our additional contribution rate at 22.4% plus £699k for the 2025/26 financial year.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 - Audited Financial Report (2025/26) & Annual Governance Statement (2025/26)
findings.headline: Council is funding capital investment through asset sales, having sold Bushloe House in 2025/26 and negotiating swimming pool sale for 2026/27
findings.detail: The council 'concluded the sale of its former offices at Bushloe House in Wigston' during 2025/26 and is 'progressing negotiations for the sale of Oadby swimming pool, with the sale expected in 2026/27.' Capital receipts increased from £1.78m combined (2024/25) to £4.661m combined (2025/26), indicating asset sales are a material funding source. This funding approach is not sustainable long-term without a portfolio of disposable assets.
findings.matters: Dependency on asset sales to fund capital investment indicates weak capital funding from mainstream sources and represents a non-renewable funding strategy that will eventually exhaust the council's asset base
findings.figures: Usable capital receipts (GF) increased from £62k to £1.512m; (HRA) from £1.718m to £3.149m; combined increase £2.881m
findings.quote: During 2025/26 the Council concluded the sale of its former offices at Bushloe House in Wigston. We have also progressed negotiations for the sale of Oadby swimming pool, with the sale expected in 2026/27.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 - Audited Financial Report (2025/26) & Annual Governance Statement (2025/26)
findings.headline: Capital programme delivered only 59% of planned spend, with HRA capital at 40% of budget
findings.detail: The council budgeted £7.199m for capital investment but spent only £4.220m, creating an underspend of £3.258m (45%). General Fund capital achieved 80% spend (£2.672m of £3.364m budget), but HRA capital performed significantly weaker at 40% (£1.548m of £3.835m budget). This capital underperformance suggests difficulty in delivering planned service improvements and housing maintenance.
findings.matters: Capital underperformance indicates the council may lack delivery capacity for planned investments and could create pressure to extend plans into future years, deferring service improvements
findings.figures: Total capital budget £7.199m, outturn £4.220m (underspend £3.258m); GF £3.364m budgeted, £2.672m spent (£692k under); HRA £3.835m budgeted, £1.548m spent (£2.287m under)
findings.quote: For 2025/26 our revenue budgets totalled £7.7 million and our capital investment programme £7.199 million.
